sections.title: The letter name
paragraphs: The letter name is (T) /tʃ/. Its main sound is heard in the word (top) /tɑp/, which means the highest part. This letter makes two spoken sounds. It can also be a silent letter.

sections.title: Mouth movements
paragraphs: For the first sound, press your tongue tip firmly on the ridge behind your upper teeth. Stop the air, then let it burst out. For the second sound, tap your tongue tip very quickly against that same ridge. Keep your voice off for the first sound, and put your voice on for the tap sound.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: You say the first sound in most words, like in (ten) /tɛn/. In American speech, you say the tap sound between two vowels before an unstressed syllable, like in (water) /wɑ.tɚ/ and (city) /sɪ.ti/. This letter is a silent letter after an s in words like (listen) /lɪ.sən/.

sections.title: Common pitfalls
paragraphs: Do not place your tongue flat against the back of your upper front teeth. Keep the tongue tip higher on the gum ridge. Do not say this letter in words where it is silent, such as (castle) /kæ.səl/. Just drop the sound completely.
